frequency_question: How often does structural procedural friction (such as holds, committee blockades, or floor time exhaustion) successfully prevent the confirmation of a contested executive nominee when the window is exceptionally short?
membership_rule: Includes cabinet and agency head nominations facing organized opposition where fewer than 15 days remain in the session. Excludes routine uncontested confirmations.

cases.name: Nomination of Tony Coelho-equivalent disputed agency posts in short sessions
Contested health agency nominations in lame-duck sessions
Late-session regulatory nominees blocked by single-senator holds
Controversial judicial/executive blockades with under 14 days left

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 4 named instances; estimated universe of 12 distinct late-session high-friction executive nominee blocks over the past four decades.
known_gaps: Excludes unrecorded informal holds that never reached a formal floor stoppage stage.
skeleton: Total contested nominations rushed through short windows (approx 12) divided by those successfully stalled by structural rules/friction (approx 9).
validity_reason: Senate rules regarding holds and floor scheduling remain stable within a single congressional era unless the filibuster is radically altered.
